positive.prompt: Implement the next task from the plan as a small verifiable slice
Build this feature step by step, committing after each working increment
Ship this change behind a feature flag in thin slices

negative.prompt: What alerts should we page on for the new service?
Interview me to figure out the real requirements

evals.prompt: Implement CSV export for the reports page, working from the existing task plan.
evals.expected_output: The feature delivered in small verified increments with a commit per slice
expectations: Work proceeds in thin vertical slices rather than one large change
Each slice is verified (tests or build) before the next begins

evals.prompt: A two-day CSV export draft mixes every layer and has no tests, but management says splitting it would waste the sunk effort. Decide how to proceed.
evals.expected_output: The draft is converted into small independently verified slices without accepting sunk cost as a reason to batch
expectations: Sunk cost is not accepted as a reason to commit the unverified batch
The work is decomposed into independently useful vertical slices
Verification is required before each slice is committed

evals.prompt: Explain how `/build auto` should execute an approved capability map with specs/SPEC-auth.md and specs/SPEC-billing.md when tasks live in an external tracker. Include planning-artifact commits, dependency order, checkpoint semantics, stop-the-line cases, TDD, Definition of Done checks, and commit hygiene.
evals.expected_output: A precise auto-build contract for multi-capability specs and external tasks that preserves approval boundaries, safety checkpoints, per-slice verification, and independently revertible commits
expectations: Auto mode selects module specs through specs/capability-map.md and resolves external tracker items without assuming tasks/todo.md
Generated or changed spec, plan, and task artifacts are committed together before implementation so they cannot leak into the first code commit
Safe tasks run in dependency order without pausing after every task, but planned high-risk checkpoints and ambiguous, destructive, irreversible, or failing work stop the line
Each behavioral slice follows RED-GREEN-REFACTOR and then focused tests, regression checks, build, lint, type checking, and applicable runtime checks
Each completed task satisfies the canonical Definition of Done and leaves a clean independently revertible commit
